workload_name: Governed manufacturing quality and maintenance workflow (reference implementation)
notes: This is an honest self-assessment of the reference implementation in this repository, not of a customer deployment. It deliberately FAILS its own release gate. A reference implementation that scored itself production-ready would be the exact failure mode the framework exists to catch, and the gap list below is more useful to a reader than a green tick would be.

scores.evidence: Hybrid local retrieval with query-time entitlement trimming; authority, freshness SLO and classification carried per passage; citation validation runs at request time and in the gate; tests/security covers ACL trimming and injected content.
scores.gap: No production index. Freshness is a field on a fixture rather than a monitored SLO per source, and there is no deletion path proven end to end from source system to index.

scores.evidence: Versioned dataset (16 cases: golden, edge, adversarial, negative, regression) executed against the real workflow, seven blocking graders with thresholds, release gate wired into CI. The gate found two genuine defects on first run.
scores.gap: Offline only. No online evaluation of sampled production traces, no canary comparison, and the model-based groundedness grader is uncalibrated so it is excluded from the blocking set.

scores.evidence: Nine planes with contract-only coupling enforced by a boundary test; explicit terminating workflow with a step budget and kill switch; sole scoped writer with idempotency and approval binding; failure modes enumerated and injected in tests.
scores.gap: No capacity model derived from measured throughput, and disaster recovery is documented rather than exercised. Rollback restores container revisions but has not been rehearsed against model, prompt and index versions together.

scores.evidence: Classification travels with every payload and passage; retention and deletion documented; corpus is entirely synthetic with a declared authority statement and owner.
scores.gap: No Microsoft Purview classification or lineage wired in. Authority is asserted in a fixture rather than inherited from a governed source, and no authoritative source has a named business owner.

scores.evidence: Cost ledger attributes spend across nine service categories per transaction and reports cost per completed task; structured logging and health, readiness and liveness endpoints exist.
scores.gap: Cost units are dimensionless demonstration units, not metered Azure spend. No service objectives are monitored, no alerts are bound to objectives, and there is no on-call rotation or incident runbook in force for a running instance.

scores.evidence: Distinct workload identity per component; managed identity only, no code path accepts a connection string; redaction applied before telemetry is written; retrieved content treated as untrusted; threat model covers injection, excessive agency, exfiltration and replay; approval binding verified by proposal fingerprint.
scores.gap: Private endpoints and network isolation are expressed in Bicep but not deployed or validated in a subscription. No independent security review or red-team exercise has been performed, and telemetry redaction has not been tested against a production-shaped payload.
